title: The Spoon Holder Takes the Lot — By Two
title_candidates: The Spoon Holder Takes the Lot — By Two
Eighty-Three and Last: Jon Baker's Kent
theme: Kent inverted the order of things: the man who had finished last in three straight TEGs led from the first afternoon and hung on by two, while the defending champion shot a course record on his way to the first Wooden Spoon of his life.
tone: house — faithful, tongue-in-cheek, British English; trivial stakes handled with grave ceremony
opening_hook: Open on the 16th green at Prince's on the final afternoon — Alex Baker, playing the best round of the tournament, signing for a 10 at the second-easiest hole on the card, and destined to finish two short — then loop back to how a man with four Wooden Spoons came to be defending a lead at all.
foreshadow: R1 at Deal: David Mullin, reigning Wooden Spoon holder, opens 40 points and 87 gross — a personal best at Royal Cinque Ports by seven shots — and is in front by the 16th hole of the tournament.
R2 at Littlestone: Alex Baker bleeds 12 shots between the 2nd and the 5th. Bank the number; it comes due on Sunday.
Two 10s and one hole number: Alex Baker takes 10 at Royal Cinque Ports' 16th in R1.
Jon Baker arrives as defending Trophy champion with back-to-back Jackets and no Spoon on his record — and is 13 shots worse than his last visit to Littlestone.

headline_candidates: Eighty-Three, a Course Record, and the Wooden Spoon

rounds.chosen_headline: Eighty-Three, a Course Record, and the Wooden Spoon
rounds.angle: Jon Baker breaks the Prince's course record with 83 and 39 points and still collects the Spoon by 12; Alex Baker's 43 — best round of the final day — comes with a 10 at the 16th and lands two short; Mullin's 37 is the worst score in the field and wins him both pots.

players.arc: Reigning Wooden Spoon holder with four to his name and Spoons in each of the last three TEGs, he opened 40 and 41 with personal bests at Deal and Littlestone, went bottom-half of the field in both closing rounds, and still walked off with the Trophy and a Jacket to add to his eight previous.

Second by two after taking 12 shots in four holes at Littlestone, an 8 at the 10th at Prince's, and 10s at the 16th in both R1 and R4 — the best final round in the field, attached to the worst arithmetic in it.

Defending Trophy champion and двух-time reigning Jacket holder who was bottom of the Spoon race from the 4th hole of R1 and never moved, then set a Prince's course record of 83 on the afternoon it was confirmed.
A personal-best gross total of +76 and course bests at Royal Cinque Ports and Prince's, undone as a Trophy contender by 27 points at Littlestone; third, and 12 clear of the Spoon.

venue_notes: TEG's 2nd visit to Kent, and four rounds of pure links: Royal Cinque Ports at Deal (2nd TEG round there, two Open Championships to its name, brutal in wind), Littlestone on the Romney Marshes (Purves, refined by Braid and MacKenzie, 2nd TEG round), then Prince's Shore/Dunes twice — the 2nd and 3rd TEG rounds at that venue, and where the course record fell. Every course was on its second visit, so TEG 13 comparisons are available everywhere and should be used: this is a tournament measured against itself a year earlier.
course_history_notes: David Mullin set a personal best on every Kent course: 87 at Royal Cinque Ports in R1 (improved by 7), 85 at Littlestone in R2 (improved by 7), 91 at Prince's in R4 (improved by 1).
Jon Baker was 13 shots worse than his last visit to Littlestone (prior best there 79 gross, TEG 13) and 7 worse at Royal Cinque Ports — before a new personal best of 83 at Prince's in R4.
Gregg Williams was 11 shots worse than his last visit to Littlestone, then posted a new personal best at Prince's: 86 gross in R3.
Alex Baker's new personal best at Royal Cinque Ports in R1 — 98 gross, improved by 4 — sat alongside being 5 shots worse than his last visit to Prince's.

trophy_storyline.subject: David Mullin's Trophy: nine ahead, home by two
trophy_storyline.why_it_matters: The man who had finished last in three consecutive TEGs led from the opening afternoon and won the main event for the third time — but only because the one man in range had already spent his cushion at Littlestone.
trophy_storyline.shape: Setup: 40 at Deal and 41 at Littlestone, best in the field both times, and the lead is nine. Turn: Prince's takes a nine off him at the 8th in R3 and an eight at the 10th in R4, he finishes bottom half of the field in both rounds, and Alex Baker closes from nine back to two. Resolution: 154 points and the Trophy by 2 — the chase ran out of holes, not out of form, and Baker's own worst round was the difference.

jacket_storyline.subject: David Mullin's Green Jacket: built at Deal and Littlestone, defended with a calculator
jacket_storyline.why_it_matters: The Jacket was the one competition nobody could argue about — Mullin beat Jon Baker head-to-head in 3 of the 4 rounds and was 12 clear by halfway.
jacket_storyline.shape: Setup: 87 and 85, best gross in the field in R1 and R2, both personal bests on the course, and the Jacket lead reaches 12. Turn: Prince's bites — 20 and 19 over par across the last two rounds, and Jon Baker's course-record 83 in R4 hauls him from 15 behind to 7. Resolution: +68, by 7, and the arithmetic was never actually in question.

spoon_storyline.subject: Jon Baker: defending champion, first-ever Wooden Spoon, and a course record on the way out
spoon_storyline.why_it_matters: He arrived as the holder of the Trophy and two straight Jackets with no Spoon anywhere on his record, and left having been bottom of the Spoon race from the 4th hole of the tournament to the last putt.
spoon_storyline.shape: Setup: 29 points at Deal after going five holes without a net par, and bottom of the pile by R1's 4th. Turn: 29 and then 28 at Prince's, with an eight at the 13th and a triple at the 17th ending his best run of the round. Resolution: a 39-point final round containing a new Prince's course record of 83 gross — birdies at the 12th and the SI 1 13th — and, an 8 at the last later, the Spoon by 12 anyway.

discovered_storylines.subject: Alex Baker's ledger of catastrophes — second place assembled from wreckage
discovered_storylines.why_it_matters: He finished two points off the Trophy while producing the loudest gross damage in the field in all four rounds, including 10s at the 16th in both R1 and R4.
discovered_storylines.shape: Setup: Deal gives him an 8 at the 11th and a 10 at the 16th, and he still opens with 37 points. Turn: Littlestone empties his pockets — 12 shots gone between the 2nd and the 5th, a nine at the 5th, an eight at the 8th — and Prince's adds an 8 at the 10th in R3. Resolution: on the final afternoon he pars the SI 1 13th, 14th and 15th, then takes 10 at the 16th, the second-easiest hole on the card, and posts the best round of the day two points too late.

discovered_storylines.subject: Gregg Williams: a personal-best gross total that bought him nothing
discovered_storylines.why_it_matters: His best-ever Gross week (+76) and two course personal bests coincided with the one round that removed him from the Trophy conversation.
discovered_storylines.shape: Setup: a nine at Deal's 3rd, and still a course-best 93. Turn: 27 points at Littlestone, 11 shots worse than his last visit there, and the Trophy is gone. Resolution: 39 points and an 86 at Prince's in R3, a triple at the 12th notwithstanding, closing from 18 off the Jacket lead to 8 — and a personal-best gross total of +76 for a tidy, unrewarded third.

payoffs.seed: Mullin the Spoon holder leading from R1 with an 87 at Deal
payoffs.resolves_in: Round 4 and 'How the three were decided'
payoffs.payoff: He posts the worst round in the field on the final day — 37 points, 19 over — and it is still enough for the Trophy and the Jacket; the three straight Spoons are formally retired.

payoffs.seed: Alex Baker bleeding 12 shots between the 2nd and 5th at Littlestone
payoffs.payoff: The final margin is 2: with a merely ordinary round in place of that one, Alex Baker wins the Trophy — the debt from R2 was never repayable.

payoffs.seed: The 10 at Royal Cinque Ports' 16th in R1
payoffs.payoff: Another 10 at another 16th — SI 17, the second-easiest hole at Prince's — ending three straight pars and the last realistic charge of the tournament.

payoffs.seed: Jon Baker as defending champion, no Spoon on his record, 13 worse than last time at Littlestone
payoffs.resolves_in: Round 4 and 'How the three were decided' (Spoon)
payoffs.payoff: The Wooden Spoon by 12 on 125 points, collected on the same afternoon he broke the Prince's course record with 83.

vehicle_fit_response.note: Taken up — a man with four Wooden Spoons and last place in three straight TEGs winning both pots is exactly the underdog frame — but it rides behind the close finish (final margin 2), which the hard rule installs as the lead frame.

why_the_champion_won: Two best-in-field rounds up front — 40 and 41, with course personal bests at Deal and Littlestone — bought a nine-point cushion he then spent almost entirely: he was bottom half of the field in R3 and R4 and won anyway, because Alex Baker had already given away more at Littlestone than he could win back, and an ordinary round in place of that one would have taken the Trophy off Mullin.
